title: MSCI Minimum Volatility Indices Methodology (January 2012)
why_used: Primary source for every USMV constraint: the 1.5%-or-20x weight cap, the 0.05% minimum holding, the +/-5% sector band, the +/-0.25 SD style band with the volatility factor exempt, the 10% one-way turnover cap, the last-business-day-of-May-and-November review, the end-of-prior-month covariance dating, and the Appendix III infeasibility ladder.
project_components: config/params.yaml usmv block; src/minvol/optimize/usmv_rules.py; src/minvol/pipeline.py (covariance lag); tests/test_constraint_satisfaction.py
redistribution_status: Copyrighted. The document carries '(c) 2012 MSCI Inc. All rights reserved.' and is not redistributed here.
retrieval_notes: Open the URL directly; it served the PDF without authentication on the access date. If the link moves, search msci.com for 'MSCI Minimum Volatility Indexes Methodology'.

title: MSCI Minimum Volatility Advanced Indexes Methodology (February 2025)
why_used: Used only to check whether the constraint set drifted over thirteen years. It did not. It also names the exempt factors as BETA and RESVOL where the 2012 text says 'the Barra Volatility risk index factor', which is the basis for the unconstrained-styles robustness variant.
redistribution_status: Copyrighted. '(c) 2025 MSCI Inc. All rights reserved.'
retrieval_notes: Open the URL directly. Note this governs the Advanced index family, not the standard one USMV tracks; it is cited for the constraint comparison only.

title: iShares MSCI USA Minimum Volatility Index Fund Summary Prospectus (Form 497K)
why_used: Fund-level confirmation of the index USMV tracks and of its inception date, filed eleven days before the fund began trading.
redistribution_status: Public domain. Works of the US federal government; EDGAR filings carry no redistribution restriction.

title: Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF Summary Prospectus (Form 497K)
why_used: Primary source for the SPLV rule in the issuer's own words: approximately 100 S&P 500 securities with the least realised volatility over the trailing one year of trading days, weighted by the inverse of each security's volatility. Also gives the fund's reported 68% annual portfolio turnover, used as a reality check on the replica's turnover.
redistribution_status: Public domain. Works of the US federal government.
retrieval_notes: EDGAR full-text search, forms=497K, query 'S&P 500 Low Volatility Index'.

title: S&P 500 Low Volatility Index methodology
why_used: Source of the quarterly rebalance calendar (February, May, August, November) and the third-Friday effective date used for the SPLV replica. The selection and weighting rules are independently confirmed by REF-004.
redistribution_status: Not retrieved. The URL returned HTTP 403 from this environment on the access date, so no copy was obtained and none is redistributed.
retrieval_notes: Available from spglobal.com/spdji under Index Methodology; registration may be required. The rebalance timing is the one parameter in this study resting on a document that could not be opened directly, and the report flags it as such.

title: Honey, I Shrunk the Sample Covariance Matrix
why_used: The constant-correlation shrinkage target and the analytic formula for the optimal shrinkage intensity. Implemented directly rather than taken from a library, because the common library implementation shrinks toward scaled identity, which is the other Ledoit-Wolf paper.
redistribution_status: Journal article, copyrighted by the publisher. A free working-paper version is available from the Barcelona School of Economics (Working Paper 92).
retrieval_notes: Published version via the Journal of Portfolio Management. Open-access working paper at bse.eu/research/working-papers/honey-i-shrunk-sample-covariance-matrix.

title: Determining the Number of Factors in Approximate Factor Models
why_used: The information criteria used to choose the number of principal components in the PCA covariance estimator, so that the factor count is determined by a criterion rather than by a round number chosen after seeing the results.
redistribution_status: Journal article, copyrighted by the publisher.
retrieval_notes: Via DOI, or the Econometric Society listing. An author copy is hosted at math.nyu.edu.

title: Betting Against Beta
author_organisation: Andrea Frazzini and Lasse Heje Pedersen
why_used: The leverage-constraint explanation for the low-volatility effect, and the factor used to test whether the replicas' alpha survives once it is controlled for. Citation details are as given by AQR in the dataset file itself.
redistribution_status: Journal article, copyrighted by the publisher. The associated dataset is distributed free by AQR under its own terms of use.
retrieval_notes: Published version via the Journal of Financial Economics; the dataset and full citation are on the AQR data library page.

title: A five-factor asset pricing model
author_organisation: Eugene F. Fama and Kenneth R. French
why_used: Defines the five factors used as the base model in the return attribution regressions.
redistribution_status: Journal article, copyrighted by the publisher.
retrieval_notes: Published version via the Journal of Financial Economics.

title: Portfolio Selection
why_used: The origin of the minimum-variance portfolio, cited here as MSCI itself cites it in the methodology document that defines the index being replicated.
redistribution_status: Journal article, copyrighted by the publisher.
retrieval_notes: Citation as given in footnote 1 of REF-001. Volume and page detail beyond 'Journal of Finance, 7' was not independently verified and is deliberately not asserted here.

title: Fama/French Data Library: 5 Factors (2x3) daily and Momentum Factor daily
why_used: Daily factor returns and the risk-free rate for the attribution regressions. The vintage used was built from the 202608 CRSP database and ends 2026-08-31, which is what limits the attribution window.
redistribution_status: Distributed free by the author for research use. Not re-hosted here; the acquisition script downloads it.
retrieval_notes: scripts/01_build_data.py downloads and caches it automatically.

title: Betting Against Beta: Equity Factors Daily
why_used: The BAB factor return series used in the second alpha regression. AQR reconstructs the full history on each update; the vintage used ends 2026-07-31, which is the binding constraint on the BAB regression window.
redistribution_status: Distributed free by AQR subject to its own terms of use. Not re-hosted here.
retrieval_notes: scripts/01_build_data.py downloads and caches it. The file is about 30 MB and is gitignored.

title: EDGAR XBRL company-facts API
why_used: Point-in-time book equity and shares outstanding, keyed on the filing date. The study uses companyfacts rather than companyconcept because the per-concept endpoint returns empty results for some filers, Coca-Cola among them.
redistribution_status: Public domain. Requires a descriptive User-Agent and a request rate at or below ten per second.
retrieval_notes: Fetched by scripts/01_build_data.py; extracted facts are cached under data/raw/sec_facts_extracted/.

title: EDGAR submissions API
why_used: The current SIC code for each registrant, which is mapped to Fama-French 12 industries for the industry factors and the sector constraint.

title: Siccodes12: Fama-French 12-industry SIC definitions
why_used: The SIC-range-to-industry mapping used to build industry dummies and the sector groups the USMV sector band is applied to.
redistribution_status: Short definitional listing distributed free by the author. Kept because the industry assignment is not reproducible without knowing the exact ranges in force.
retrieval_notes: Downloaded by scripts/01_build_data.py; the preserved copy records the version actually used.

title: 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (DGS10)
author_organisation: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)
why_used: Collected for the optional rate-sensitivity extension. It is not used by any result reported in the main analysis, and is listed here because the acquisition script fetches it.
redistribution_status: Public domain source series from the US Treasury, redistributed by FRED.

title: Daily price and volume history
author_organisation: Yahoo Finance (accessed via the yfinance library)
why_used: Split-adjusted closes, dividend-adjusted closes and volume for every constituent, plus USMV, SPLV and SPY. The source of the survivorship gap the study measures: delisted companies return no data at all.
redistribution_status: Not redistributed. Terms of use do not permit republishing the price history.
retrieval_notes: scripts/01_build_data.py downloads it. Note that Yahoo back-adjusts the close for splits, which is why src/minvol/data/splits.py exists.

title: S&P 500 Historical Components and Changes
why_used: The point-in-time index membership panel. Cross-checked against REF-019; the two agreed on 497 of 503 current names, with the six differences being index changes inside the gap between the panel's as-of date and the Wikipedia snapshot.
redistribution_status: MIT licensed upstream. Not vendored here; the loader clones it and records the commit hash so a run is reproducible against a specific vintage.
retrieval_notes: git clone https://github.com/fja05680/sp500. The raw.githubusercontent and codeload hosts were unreachable from this environment, which is why a clone is used.

title: List of S&P 500 companies
why_used: Independent snapshot of current index membership, used solely to cross-check REF-018. It validates the panel's endpoint and cannot validate its history, which the reconciliation output states.
redistribution_status: CC BY-SA. Not redistributed; the loader caches the page under data/raw/.
